stem: A hospital reviews results from the AHRQ Hospital Survey on Patient Safety Culture (SOPS). What is the most appropriate use of these results?

options.A: Identify strengths and areas for improvement in the organization’s patient-safety culture and guide improvement work.
options.B: Use the survey as the sole basis for disciplining individual employees.
options.C: Treat the survey as a diagnostic test for individual clinical competence.
options.D: Ignore unit-level patterns because the survey is not intended for organizational improvement.

rationale: AHRQ’s Hospital SOPS assesses staff perceptions of patient-safety culture across domains such as teamwork, staffing and work pace, response to error, communication, and handoffs. AHRQ recommends using SOPS results to identify strengths and areas for improvement.
educational_objective: Use safety-culture survey data appropriately for organizational improvement.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
source_document_title: SOPS Hospital Survey 2.0; SOPS Frequently Asked Questions
source_locator: Hospital SOPS purpose and FAQ—assess safety culture; identify strengths and areas for improvement
source_claim_supported: Hospital SOPS measures staff perceptions of patient-safety culture and supports identification of strengths and improvement opportunities.
correction_summary: Rebuilt the original generic engagement-survey item around an authoritative AHRQ safety-culture instrument.
audit_findings: Distractors misuse the survey for individual discipline/competence or ignore its improvement role.
Independent second pass found a unique answer.
